deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of the 'geometric representation' section of Riemann's Inaugural Dissertation (1851). In the printed text it is part of the final articles (around Art. 21) that lead to the mapping theorem. Here it is numbered §.14c. The previous page (§16 draft) belongs to the Dirichlet-principle argument; the next page continues the analysis of the minimizing function ω and its singularities. This page contains no computations, only definitions and qualitative claims about the image surface.

Setup (heading rewritten to 'Wir betrachten jetzt die geometrische Darstellung einer Function von z'): w = u + iv is a function of z = x + iy defined on a bounded surface T spread over the plane A. Each point O of T is assigned the point Q of a second plane B whose rectangular coordinates are (u, v).

Claim 1. The totality of the points Q can be regarded as forming a surface S over B. To each point of S corresponds one point O of T that moves continuously with it. This 'one' is the printed text's 'ein einziger'. In modern terms, S is the Riemann surface of the image, i.e. T pulled forward by w, and w : T -> S is a bijective, bicontinuous identification.

Claim 2 (rewritten several times). The final intended form is as follows.
- By assumption 1, no connection can exist between parts of S unless the corresponding parts of T are connected.
- Conversely, if w is everywhere continuous in T, the parts of S can be given the same connection as the corresponding parts of T. So S and T have the same connectivity (Zusammenhang); in modern terms they are homeomorphic via w.
- The boundary of S corresponds partly to the boundary of T and partly to the discontinuity points of w.
- Riemann announces that he will show that the hypotheses made in Art. 5 for T hold for S as well.
- The first part, continuity of correspondence, 'obviously' could fail only if T had the same property, contrary to hypothesis. The second part 'shall be proved at once'.

Claim 3. In the interior, S is everywhere schlicht over B, apart from possibly isolated points. No 'Spaltung' (splitting/branching along a line) and no 'Umfaltung' (folding over) occurs. In modern terms, a non-constant holomorphic map is open and orientation-preserving. Its Jacobian u_x v_y − u_y v_x = |w'(z)|^2 is ≥ 0. Hence the image surface has no fold lines. Branching (ramification) occurs at most at isolated points where w' = 0, where it is locally like ζ^n.

Nothing is computed. The page serves to set up the image-surface language used for the conformal-mapping theorem at the end of the dissertation.
errors: No computational errors (there are no computations).
Claim 1 (a unique preimage for each point of S) is a definition/assumption, not a consequence: it only holds by construction, by treating S as a multi-sheeted surface where w is not injective.
The argument that the connectivity of S matches that of T is only sketched ('offenbar'); the converse direction is announced as 'sogleich bewiesen', not proved here.
The 'no folds' claim implicitly uses w' ≠ 0 or the open-mapping/orientation property; Riemann gives no justification on this page.
The text is heavily reworked: several alternative formulations of claim 2 coexist, partly contradictory in wording before cancellation.

results.what: Representation of a complex function w=u+iv on T by the image surface S in the w-plane B, with points of S in continuous one-to-one correspondence with points of T
results.modern_name: Image Riemann surface / w as a homeomorphism T -> w(T) as covering surface; geometric representation of an analytic function as a mapping

results.what: Connectivity (Zusammenhang) of S equals that of T when w is continuous; boundary of S comes from the boundary of T and from discontinuities of w
results.modern_name: Topological invariance of connectivity under homeomorphism

results.what: Interior of the image surface is locally schlicht: no folding (Umfaltung) and no splitting along lines, at most isolated exceptional (branch) points
results.modern_name: Open mapping / orientation preservation of holomorphic maps; isolated ramification points
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1851 (geometric form); open mapping theorem made rigorous later (Weierstrass school etc.)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of a passage that appears in essentially this form in Riemann's published 1851 dissertation (the geometric representation leading to the mapping theorem). The only novelty is the draft's section numbering (§14c) and wording variants, which are of philological interest.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y',real=True); z=x+I*y; w=expand(z**2); u=re(w); v=im(w); simplify(diff(u,x)*diff(v,y)-diff(u,y)*diff(v,x) - 4*(x**2+y**2))
checkable.asserts: The Jacobian of a holomorphic map equals |w'|^2 ≥ 0 (here w=z^2: Jacobian = 4|z|^2), so no orientation reversal ('Umfaltung') occurs; it vanishes only at the isolated point z=0.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y',real=True); u=x**2-y**2; v=2*x*y; simplify(diff(u,x)-diff(v,y)), simplify(diff(u,y)+diff(v,x))
checkable.asserts: u, v satisfy the Cauchy–Riemann equations, which underlie the claim that S is locally schlicht in the interior.
The non-holomorphic map conj(z) has Jacobian −1 < 0 (orientation reversal); this contrast shows why the 'no folding' property is specific to analytic w.

transcription_corrections: Second line: the corrected sense is approximately 'Wir lassen jedem Punkte O der Fläche T, in welchem w einen bestimmten Werth hat, den Punkt Q der Ebene B entsprechen, dessen rechtwinklige Coordinaten u, v sind'. The garbled '{+jedenen [?] w zu+}' is likely a fragment of 'jedem ... w ... zuordnen'.
'zwischen drei Theilen von S' should almost certainly read 'zwischen den Theilen von S' (cf. the rewritten version 'zwischen den Flächentheilen von S').
'[-Wortsatz-] Satz' / 'Wortsätzen' are likely 'Voraussetzung' / 'Voraussetzungen' (cf. 'Der in 1. gemachten Voraussetzung nach').
'die in Art S für T gemachten' should read 'die in Art. 5 für T gemachten Voraussetzungen'.
In claim 1, 'jedem Punkt ein Punkt in T' should likely read 'jedem Punkte ein einziger in T mit ihm stetig fortrückender Punkt O' (matching the printed dissertation).

'Ersteres können offenbar der T überall entsprechende Zusammenhang...' is a conflation of cancelled and uncancelled text. The intended sense is approximately 'Ersteres könnte offenbar nur eintreten, wenn T dieselbe Eigenschaft hätte, der Annahme zuwider'.
Last paragraph: 'Begrenzungen' is doubtful; the sense is 'Im Innern aber ist S, abgesehen von einzelnen Punkten, überall schlicht über B, d.h. es findet keine Spaltung und keine Umfaltung statt'.
